statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the very price path this score measures. Stress rises to 52 in the elevated band on a verified escalation in the Red Sea: Houthi forces took Yemen's Perim island on Friday after seizing the port of Mokha, completing their control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait through which the shut East-West pipeline's Red Sea exports must pass, and their spokesman exempted Saudi ships from the safe-navigation assurance. Offsetting that, President Trump said on Saturday the war should end soon after November's midterm elections. Confidence is 86 on a complete evidence set verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly five hours after the final slot of this horizon closes, so no slot contains a tradeable session and no danger window is published. Third, a geopolitical development is not a price path: the Bab el-Mandeb seizure is a supply-channel constraint that belongs in Stress until a live session shows persistent one-way Nasdaq structure. Stress rises to 52 because triple-digit crude, a shut 4-5 million barrel per day pipeline with no repair timeline, a compromised Red Sea outlet and a 16 September FOMC decision priced at roughly an 87% chance of a 25 basis point increase are all unresolved into next week. Stress alone does not change the mapped state.
headline: Twenty-one hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, while the constraint around Saudi crude tightened at the second chokepoint: Houthi forces seized Perim island on Friday to complete control of the Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea gateway serving Yanbu, even as the East-West pipeline that feeds it stays shut with no published repair timeline and Washington signalled the war should end after the November midterms.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend, and was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high, roughly 4.5% under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95%, and Friday's reporting had the 10-year finishing just below 5%. WTI is marked $100.05, down 2.37% on the day but up 9.7% on the week and 20.15% on the month, with Brent $104.61, down 2.81%.

The material new development this hour concerns the second chokepoint rather than the first. Houthi forces reached Yemen's Perim island on Friday, one day after taking the Red Sea port of Mokha, completing their control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait after government forces withdrew. That matters directly to the existing outage: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is the Hormuz bypass, it terminates at Yanbu on the Red Sea, and its exports must then transit Bab el-Mandeb. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on Friday evening that navigation is safe for all companies except Saudi ships, which are already banned. The bypass and the bypass's outlet are therefore both constrained at the same time, which is why Stress rises rather than continuing to decay.

The de-escalation channel remains real and is what keeps the increase to a single point. Saudi Arabia condemned the drone strike on the East-West pipeline in the strongest terms but agreed not to retaliate for now at Baghdad's request, while reserving the right to take all necessary measures. Iraq confirmed the drones were launched from Maysan province, dismissed the province's operations commander, ordered an investigation and closed the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran. President Trump said on Saturday that the war in Iran will likely end soon after November's midterm elections and that energy prices would then fall sharply, while also saying Iran was likely responsible for the pipeline attack. An Iran-Oman shared-route agreement is reported for signature in Muscat on Monday. The pipeline itself, 1,200km carrying 4-5 million barrels a day or roughly 4-5% of global supply, remains shut with no published repair timeline, though an April attack on the same line took three days to restore.

The policy layer is the other unresolved exposure. Friday's August CPI ran 3.4% year over year with core at 0.3% month over month, above the 0.2% consensus, and the CME FedWatch tool closed near an 87% chance of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC, up from about 72% the previous day. Preliminary September Michigan sentiment came in at 47.8 against a 51 consensus. A policy tightening priced into an energy-led inflation shock is an environment problem, not an observed no-retracement price path, so under the risk definitions it belongs in Stress and Confidence rather than in Tail.

Shared Finviz context collected at 16:33 UTC was about two hours old at assessment time and carried a partial collection status with the calendar section unavailable, so it fell outside the freshness and completeness gate and was used for headline discovery only. Every material story it surfaced was re-verified against primary reporting before it affected any score, and no part of it was treated as evidence of live Nasdaq structure. Full independent research was carried out regardless.

Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure, so conditional Tail rises only from 6 to a ceiling of 13 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates, and no slot approaches the 25-point block threshold. The Sunday reopen and Monday's Muscat signing both lie beyond this horizon and are carried as checkpoints, not as scored paths. The next assessment that sees a live session will score the observed path: a wide reopen gap that holds near its extreme with shallow or failed retracements would be the evidence required to lift Tail, whereas orderly two-way price discovery would not.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 18:00 UTC on 11 September to 17:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens inside the U.S. afternoon that followed Friday's inflation print, with Tail between 13 and 17 in mixed mode and Stress in the high band near 78 decaying as the event passed and volatility fell. Tail dropped to 7 at the 21:00 UTC futures halt and has since held a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across the final twenty slots, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress fell monotonically from 78 to 50 across the twenty-four hours, and Confidence held inside the high band throughout, between 85 and 89. No slot in the window reached the 25-point Tail block threshold.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly five hours after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps through 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 to a ceiling of 13 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs from 52 down to a floor of 48 through the overnight quiet, then climbs back to 53 as the Gulf session, the Monday Muscat signing and the reopen approach with their outcomes unknown. Mode stays normal until the final three slots, where it becomes mixed to reflect a genuinely two-sided conditional gap distribution. Confidence decays from 86 to 80 purely as a function of distance from the last verified market observation. The conditions that would change this picture are observable only after the reopen: a wide gap that holds near its extreme, shallow or failed retracements, and repeated extension.
